I posted this in response to another thread. I wanted to give it its own thread since I detailed it all out. It's s system of moderation which could be implemented here that would check and balance moderators and help assure that the site is a system that works for the userbase as a whole and not a place for multiple smaller dictatorships which use the userbase at their will in their respective subverses. Hopefully this is of some use.

This is something I always wanted to see in Reddit. It would have been the best added feature IMO, had it happened. I think we need to take some ideas out of our real lives to apply this. I have a pretty good idea about how to get this done which will not depend on who is subscribed to which subverse or Admin intervention. It will be a system by the Voaters, for the Voaters.

Similar to how nations have a system of law in hierarchy, we can have a hierarchy of moderation. It will have similarities to governmental systems but will not copy any one government exactly. It will require help from the admins to implement. I think a rough outline can be as follows:

Atko is the King. This is his land and he rules it as he sees fit. We will trust him to be a good king and rule it wisely.

Admins are similar to national supreme court justices here in the US. They don't get voted in or out. They are appointed and are in for life or until they resign. They have full control over how the site operates and have final say on all matters. The rest goes without saying as they are more or less employees of the website. We will also trust them.

We will develop a new subverse which will be similar to a jurisdictional court, however the jurisdiction will be the entire website. This subverse will be in charge of checking the moderation team of other subverses. Similar to a supreme court, they have override abilities to the moderation team of a subverse, but only by an appeals system. They must not interfere with the goings on of a subverse unless addressed by users of Voat. Even in these cases, they will be called upon to decide appropriate courses of action based on 1) The general rules of Voat, 2) The general rules of the subverse, 3) What seems fair to them based on the rights of the users (after all, all rules need to be addressed occasionally to determine their continued effectiveness).

These will basically be the moderators of the moderation teams of subverses. Their responsibility will be to the userbase, not subordinate moderation teams. They will be voted on by the userbase as a whole on an interval which is yet to be determined. They will carry an UNLIMITED amount of term possibilities (This is important). The reason for this is because here on the internet, things move faster than real life. Changes are passed in a matter of days/weeks rather than years/decades. We only need the best moderators for this job, regardless of how long they've been doing the job. If we impose term caps on this position, changes can/may be made so quickly that it may distort the overall view and direction of Voat. We need moderators here who are effective at keeping and sustaining the core values of the site. To do this we may need a moderator who has been here for years. This moderation team will be checked/balanced by the userbase as a whole by voting. They will convene at an interval yet to be determined or at any time necessary between that interval. This moderation team will have a specified amount of moderators. Decisions will be passed based on a minimum amount of votes, and a majority system. Any moderators inactive for an undetermined period of time may be relieved of their position.

The moderators of this subverse will NOT be called for the following reasons:

  • Unbanning a user from a subverse (however a user may be unbanned as a result of related action)
  • Taking posts out of any spam filter
  • Implementing new rules/regulations to a subverse
  • Deciding an overall plan for a subverse and what type for content the subverse will contain
  • etc.

They WILL be called for the following:

  • Deciding whether current policies in a subverse are generally unfair to the userbase as a whole and repealing them if necessary
  • Deciding whether a specific moderator or moderation team is infringing on basic rights of the userbase
  • Deciding whether a specific moderator or moderation team is abusing their power and must be relieved of their position
  • etc.

Another idea would be to have this moderation team be responsible for multiple moderation teams under this one, but above the subverse moderators, who are responsible for a number of subverses based on the # of subscribers. These moderation teams would also have unlimited term caps and be voted on at an interval which is yet to be determined, and not necessarily the same as the moderation team above it. This reason is twofold:

  • Subverses with a larger amount of subscribers may operate differently than subverses with a smaller amount of subscribers
  • To alleviate the load of a huge amount of subverses all on one moderation team and to spread out the work

This idea can be implemented immediately or at a time in which the load of the website has grown and this system is needed.

The last group of moderators would be subverse specific. This group would function the same way it operates now. They will be chosen and kept as the subverse sees fit but will ultimately be responsible for the userbase as a whole and will answer to the moderation team directly superior to them.

This system will serve as a method to have subverses act independently but still be responsible for their actions. It will allow for a system of balance between the users and moderators.

Subverses will NOT fall into the jurisdiction of any moderation team below the admins if:

  • They have UNDER a specified amount of subscribers (amount yet to be determined)
  • They are operated by a single user for his/her own purposes (Ex: compiled works of that user). The subverse in question would have to be moderated BY the user in which it is about, however.
  • It is private (other limitations may apply)

This system can be modified before and after it is put in place. The intent and purpose of this system is NOT so that things will stay the same indefinitely. All things must change with the times. The intent and purpose for this system IS for consistency in fairness to the users.

An option would also be to have a subverse which will act as a council to make changes to and oversee this system. The council will be in charge of adding/removing checking/balancing the moderation team directly below the admins, but will NOT have any jurisdiction over any decisions made regarding the oversight of subverses directly nor make any changes to any subverses. The council will SOLELY be in charge of modifying and upholding the system. The council will be in charge of making decisions based on any discrepancy of the system. The council will be voted in and will have an undetermined amount of term limits (an unlimited term cap is a possibility, however an alternative term cap may be imposed). The council may convene at an interval yet to be determined or at any time necessary between that interval. This council will have a specified amount of moderators. Decisions will be passed based on a minimum amount of votes, and a majority system. Any moderators inactive for an undetermined period of time may be relieved of their position.

Please discuss. Any thoughts regarding this system are appreciated. Maybe we can work something like this into place. I know it sounds complicated and time consuming, but the idea is that 1) It will work as a system which checks itself and is best for the users, and 2) hopefully will not be as time consuming as one would hope as responsibilities are displaced on their respective moderation team.
[Repost for visibility] I've created a democratic method of moderation that limits power with checks and balances for moderators - complete with user input.

One thing I think is important: NOBODY can be banned from the court subverses. If (by which I mean when) problematic and habitually unhelpful users arrive, they can be flagged as such by the community or mods there and have their posts/comments covered with something along the lines of "This user's contributions are hidden for so and so reasons; click here to see what they have to say" and their flagged status can be appealed and reverted if they change tune.

The main issue with what is currently happening to reddit, and what we absolutely need to avoid here, is the opacity and whimsy of authoritative action. While I have nothing against normal subverse moderators being able to impose bans as they see fit to maintain a healthy community, having moderation logs public should be a great help to ensuring that stays a generally proper environment. However, for the voat-wide judges, we need to have absolute faith in their actions and the ability to verify that said faith is not being betrayed, so full-out stifling of speech cannot be allowed; it can only be hidden with the option to ignore the cover at the users' discretion. These actions should also have the name of the moderator who executed them attached, IMO.

I think a hierarchical system is a good idea. While we only need one Supreme Court of users above all but admins/Atko, they also don't need to hear every single thing, so circuit courts below them would fill that role. Subverses can request judicial attachment when they reach sufficient size -- and moderators OR COMMUNITY MEMBERS can make this request -- and a circuit court will choose to adopt the subverse. If no court wants to because of load, a new court is made. Then if a trial is disputed, it can be handled by either requesting a different circuit court to come in, or kicking it up the chain to the Supreme Court. I believe this system would work well by fostering cooperation between subverse moderators and judges, while also severely reducing the risk of cronyism between the same.

Also, while a user can be both a subverse mod and a judge simultaneously, they cannot serve on a court with jurisdiction over their subverse without giving up moderator ability for the duration of their term as judge. Perhaps give them no permissions on their subverse without removing them from the list entirely?

I also wouldn't mind seeing voat-wide and subverse constitutions or codes of conduct implemented. For subverses, this would be optional, and for a voat-wide, it would have to be something like, say, the US Constitution (I'm an American, so I'm most familiar with that one). Short, easily extensible, and only covering the bare minimum. As with all things, if the community of a subverse takes issue with their constitution/code they can demand alteration and handle that internally or through the court system, and the voat constitution would be subject to amendment with global voting and review.

I'm not sure how to go about staving off both tyranny of the majority and oligarchy, but I think I'd have to side with the community over a cabal, with the stipulation that the majority can also be fought by smaller parties, and the courts are there to serve as intercessors in that regard.

Again, to define this system in its simplest terms: This is at its most outreaching effort a method to keep consistency and balance to site wide moderation. The problem I see with any online community that holds elections (i.e. voting for moderators, etc.) is the vast potential for hostile takeover. Voat is far from the largest online community - it wouldn't take much for a group from an opposing community to come in, vote in a plant, then destroy the place. There's also the issue with vote manipulation (one account ≠ one person necessarily). Sure there could be ways to reduce the possibility of this (votes of longer-standing subscribers or more active subscribers count more or whatever), but any system can be gamed. Personally I'm in favour of benevolent dictatorship.

Not that I'm overlooking everything else you said, but although I agree that most things can be gamed, I just wanted to point out that Voat runs votes by IP rather than by account. As you said, it helps, but nothing is foolproof. I was playing with the idea of votes only counting from active members with accounts which are at least X [months?] old.

IP monitoring stops your average troll/enemy, but not a tech savvy one. With a little money it isn't hard to rent a bot net (assuming nobody in a large community doesn't already have access to one). Making users have accounts that are (for example) 6 months old only slows the attack down by 6 months.

The other thing to consider is internal attacks. We're welcoming everyone here, so what happens when there are two opposing communities on Voat which have a large size disparity? Would it not be possible for one to effectively vote brigade the election of the other?

Hopefully we'll be able to rely on the admins for support with voting. The bylaws of The System can be setup but the method it gets done will be implemented by multiple people based on their knowledge. I'm less knowledgeable about exactly how we'd be able to prevent abuse of the voting. Hopefully this aspect can be handled by someone more familiar.

Concerning opposing communities, I'm not sure exactly how much relevance this would play. Remember, the purpose of The System isn't a method of raising the awareness or position of any one community or group. The purpose is solely for oversight of subordinate moderation staff. The System is meant to be equal to all on the site. Subverse moderators will be trusted to regulate their activity as they see fit. The System will only act if those subverse moderators aren't doing their jobs effectively or by the (possible future) guidelines of Voat.

Realistically, by implementing this, nothing should change as far as users are concerned. They should only be comfortable knowing that moderators are responsible for their actions. Dictatorships won't be taken out of hand here. That's the goal.

It sounds like you are definitely on to something. Many subverses, especially the more general-interest, popular ones, definitely should not be the fiefs of whoever happened to create them first. I'm also thinking there should be a general blueprint for subverse constitutions that each subverse can apply to themselves with modification. Or, if there's enough confidence in voting, implied constitutions would evolve organically out of past voting decisions (UK political system-style).

Although I would support subverse specific constitutions 100%, my only concern is that by focusing on this, it may over complicate the issue at hand.

Further, if a subverse specific constitution were to be in place, only that subverses moderators would be obligated by its guidelines. While I support this as a clear and consistent method for moderators to manage their specific subverses, it would have little bearing to The System as circuit court moderators would be bound by the site-wide constitution rather than the rules the subverse moderators have put in place for their subverses. I think subverse specific constitutions would serve more as a method of uderstanding of how a subverse operates for circuit moderators than a basis for decision making.
